column1: # The igMetaObject / igMetaField object model — methods named from their bodies.
# These are curated, not generated: each name comes from decompiling the function
# and reading it against the reflection structs in data/reflection.json (which give
# every field's name and offset).  Kept out of the generated overlays on purpose —
# a generator cannot infer these, a reader can.
# igMetaField — the field's technique dispatcher and name mangling.
#   `_isAlikeShallowMethod` (+0x2c) each hold a technique number 0-3; the three
#   8-byte thunks load that byte into a3 and jump to the common dispatcher.
#   +0x18 -> igMetaObject +0x1c, and +0x0c), and finds a field by that name across
# igMetaObject — construction and the bookkeeping fields.
# Second pass: children/field bookkeeping and the object construction path.
#   +0x30 _instances; igObject's MetaObject is fetched through vtable +0x58.
# calls the registrar, then invokes every vfunc of the returned object and
# releases it — the static-initialiser runner the class accessors call.
# stores the class's _vTablePointer into the new instance and initialises it.
# bumps the MetaObject's _instanceCount and appends to _instances.
# `*obj = &0x52f0f0` (igObject's vtable) + header flags; the temp GetVTable builds.
# Third pass: the igMetaField base, igMetaObject, and igMemoryPoolInfo.
# The whole 0x2fa000-0x300000 run is the object model.  Three vtables anchor it:
# plus the two memory-ref metafields 0x532a50 / 0x52f330.  The 100+ subclasses
# share these methods through their own vtables, so most of the addresses below
# occur as the same slot in dozens of tables (e.g. 0x2fc210 at +0x08 of every
# every field, and the offsets it reads (+0x14 _handleName, +0x18 _aliasedTo,
# _releaseMessages, +0x50 _eventTrackerCapacity) are exactly those of the class
# igMetaField (vtable 0x52f230) -- field offsets are those of igMetaField in
#   the constructor: the igObject constructor, the vtable, then _Init; every
#   derived MetaField's constructor calls it.  (MWCC emits the pair -- a
#   constructor that sets the vtable and an explicit `_Init` body, exactly as
#   the body: every field to its default (_typeIndex 0xffff, _persistent 1,
#   the alike techniques 0/1/2); every `<X>MetaField_GetVTable` calls it.
#   the copy constructor: vtable, then each field from the source, duping
#   vtable slot +0x08: releases _default (+0x20) and chains to the base slot --
#   the destructor path FUN_002ff820 runs as `(**(code **)(*obj + 8))()`.
#   vtable slot +0x8c: sizes _default for the field's type, then copies the
#   argument in -- sets the field's default value.
#   dispatches on +0x24 _resetMethod to the technique slots +0x70/+0x74/+0x78.
#   returns +0x10 _typeIndex; when it is -1, asks the +0x5c type slot for its
#   aligns its argument up to the size the +0x6c slot reports.
#   dispatches an explicit technique to the copy slots +0x90/+0x94/+0x98/
#   +0x9c/+0xa0; the three 8-byte thunks below pass +0x27/+0x28/+0x29, so each
#   copy kind has its own entry point.
#   field's own value string, via its +0xe4 slot.
#   base constructor, then the vtable, igMetaObject_Init, and the _metaFields
#   copy constructor: the igObject copy constructor, the vtable, +0x1c _name
#   by +0x60 _poolName and runs the instance initialiser on it; the pool-aware
#   The intermediate class is igRefMetaField: its two fields, +0x34 _construct
#   clears.  igMemoryRefMetaField's ctor calls the igRefMetaField ctor first,
#   then sets its own vtable (its fields +0x38 _memSize, +0x3c _memType, +0x40
#   the factory the reflection field ctor for an igMemoryRef field calls:
#   allocates 0x50 bytes and constructs, or goes through the class's MetaObject.
# Fourth pass: the igMemoryRefMetaField slot roles and igMemoryPoolInfoList.
# THE VTABLE SLOT MAP (read off 0x532a50 = igMemoryRefMetaField and 0x52f330 =
# igMemoryRefArrayMetaField; both tables are 0x100 bytes, and the 27-slot
# igMemoryPoolInfoList table 0x5329e0 ends at +0x6c, so the igMemoryRefMetaField
# table that follows it is a separate one).  Slots below +0x54 are the embedded
# igObject interface; +0x54 is Gap::Core::igObject::vfunc_19.  igMetaField's own
#   +0x64 GetTypeSize            (the class override differs per field class)
#   +0x7c/80    construct / destruct the instance's value in place (the base
#             0x2fd050/0x2fd060 are no-ops -- a scalar field has no lifecycle)
#             three method numbers to 0, and the technique-0 body 0x2fc9d0 is a
#   +0xac Write to the IGB writer (base 0x2fcea0 returns 0 when _persistent,
#             0x2fcec0 dispatches a3 0/1/2/3 there; +0xb4 0x2fcf90 is a byte
#   +0xc8/cc    the field-value (de)serialisation pair; the base bodies are
#             the two directions of `memcpy` around _size, each calling the
#   +0xd0       the hook +0xc8/+0xcc call after a transfer
# (see igMemoryRefMetaField_Init), so it selects reset technique +0x74 (a no-op
# in this class!) and copy technique 2 -- the +0x70 and +0x90 overrides below are
# taken by a direct +0x70 call and by the deep/construct method numbers, not by
# the two dispatchers.  That _resetMethod 3 vs the +0x74 no-op is an open
#   the instance value is allocated from the field's _memType (+0x3c): element
#   the element count is `_memSize / elementSize` or, for the array subclass,
#   vtable +0x70: release the instance's value (element refs, and the buffer
#   when _releaseOnReset), then install a refcounted clone of _default there.
#   vtable +0x90, copy technique 0 -- the one _deepCopyMethod and
#   _constructCopyMethod select: release the destination, clone the source (per
#   element where the memory type is named), then re-addref the elements.
#   vtable +0x98, copy technique 2 and the class's _shallowCopyMethod: release
#   the destination, clone the source, re-addref the elements.
#   vtable +0xa4: prints each element with the field's own value format
#   (0x4faef0) instead of the scalar one igMetaField_Print uses.
#   vtable +0xa8: walks the instance's elements (count from _memSize / element
#   size) and runs each element's +0x48 slot plus the recursive release 0x300b00.
#   vtable +0xac: writes the field into the IGB writer -- _persistent gates it,
#   then FUN_002d8a80 creates the member from _memType, _alignmentType and the
#   pool name (the array subclass instead writes every element).
#   instance values element by element through 0x300820.
#   igMetaField_Init): equal element counts and a byte compare of the contents.
#   +0x4c _poolName: the setter interns the name through the string cache
#   (0x2eb010/0x2eaf60) and refcounts the old one; the getter returns it.
#   +0x44 _alignmentType: resolves an alignment-type name through the context's
#   type list (0x586dd0) and stores its index, or -1 when the name is null.
#   the non-virtual refcount helpers over an instance's element array: +1 each
#   element's refcount (the low 23 bits of the word at +4 are the count), and
#   -1 with a release through 0x2ff820 when it reaches zero.
#   the shared array allocator the memory-ref construct path and the two
#   array-reserve paths call: `count * elementSize` bytes with the memory type's
#   alignment, zeroed when the pool asks for it, stored at the field's _offset.
#   Its callers pass three different field instances (the reflection prototypes
#   0x562498/0x5624a0, and a field resolved with igMetaObject_GetFieldAt), so the
#   prefix names the family the helper serves rather than one owner.
# growable list of memory-pool infos: the engine keeps two of them in the globals
# 0x586f58/0x586f60 (created by FUN_002f2180, destroyed by FUN_002f2200) and hands
# out entries through FUN_002f0370.  None of these are vtable entries; the two
# 32-byte wrappers are the list's allocator/deallocator, both calling the context
# memory pool at 0x586dc8+0x30 through its +0xd8 (allocate) and +0x108 (release)
# igMetaEnum (handle 0x585d60, vtable 0x532b50): the named value/flag table the
# engine's enum fields and "pool option" tables are built from.  reflection.json
# {NOT_SET=0, CUBE_MAP=1, SPHERE_MAP=2} from the rodata at 0x4d4ce0/0x485bf0.
# The class has no overrides: all nine are plain methods.
#   interns `_name`, builds the two lists and fills them.
#   returns `_names`' element count; `_names[index]` as a refcounted string;
#   the two lookups: by name over `_names` (returns the matching `_values` entry)
#   and by value over `_values` (returns the matching name).
#   the two debug-printing helpers (both take the enum as the last argument):
#   append the name of every value whose bit is set in `mask`, joined by a space
#   (0x4f9950 — a single blank, not a '|'), and copy one value's name into a
# igMetaField's raw-field-memory transfer slots: the IGB binary serializer's
# per-field read and write, in the field's own inline representation.  The
# argument order is the same for both — (field, field_memory, stream, ...) — and
# only the copy direction differs, so +0xc8 copies field -> stream and +0xcc
# stream -> field; each then runs the +0xd0 hook on the destination (the base
# +0xd0, 0x2fd170, byte-swaps each `_size`-byte element, which is the endian
# swap this transfer needs).  The engine's own name survives in the +0xc8
# directory\nDid you modify the object after adding it to the directory ?\n"
# (0x4fafd0/0x4fb050) — a raw-ref write must be able to resolve the pointer into
# the output directory, which is exactly what the +0xc8 override does
# (`FUN_002d7c50` pointer -> index, writing 0xffffffff when it is not in the
# directory).  The +0xcc override is its mirror: it reads the index and installs
# the resolved pointer (`FUN_002d7e90`) plus the element's `_memType` (+0x3c).
# The base bodies are the inverse memcpys; the array class loops them over `_num`
# The four `GetSize` overrides and the base `SetToDefault`, read off the field
# allocation by the *same* slot on the memory type (`_memType`+0x3c), so +0x64 is
# the field's byte size and every concrete field class overrides it: the base
# and `igMemoryRefArrayMetaField` returns `_num * 4` (one pointer per element of
# the inline array), truncated to the u16 `_size` field.  The base +0x70 is the
# same virtual the ref class overrides with `igMemoryRefMetaField_SetToDefault`
#: it copies `_default` (+0x20) over the instance's value at `_offset`.
#   the +0xd0 technique is a byte reversal of each `_size`-byte element of a
#   buffer (`t6 = _size` at +0x14; for each element, swap byte i with byte
#   `ReadRawFieldMem` run on the destination after their copy.  +0xd4 is the
#   in-place form: it byte-swaps this field's own value in an instance
#   `_memType` learning -- a plain reference has no element type to learn.
# The base `igMetaField` implementation of the slots whose subclass overrides are
# already named, so the virtual is identified by its counterpart rather than by a
# guess: the ref class overrides `+0x7c`/`+0x80` with ConstructValue/DestructValue,
# `+0xa8` with ReleaseElements and `+0xac` with Write, and the base bodies are the
# no-ops / the `_persistent` stub those override.  (The copy and alike technique
# slots are NOT named this way: their *dispatch thunks* already carry the method
# the technique bodies at `+0x90`/`+0x94`/`+0x98`/`+0xb4`..`+0xc0` cannot take them.)
#   +0xac: m2c's ReadRawFieldMem counterpart -- base returns 0 when the field is
#   `_persistent` and -1 otherwise; the ref class replaces it with the IGB writer.
#   the class destructor slot (+0x08).  igMetaField_Destruct is the body; each
#   subclass whose vtable needs its own entry carries a `j` thunk to it.
#   +0xf0: the construct flag -- the base returns 0 (the generic object initialiser
#   constructs a plain field's value), and igRefMetaField returns its own
